title: Boerse Stuttgart obtains DLT trading and settlement system license
summary: Boerse Stuttgart Group is the first exchange group in Europe to obtain the DLT Trading and Settlement System (TSS) license under the DLT Pilot Regime.
content: Boerse Stuttgart Group has become the first exchange group in Europe to receive a DLT Trading and Settlement System license under the European Union's DLT Pilot Regime. This regulatory approval allows the group to operate a DLT-based infrastructure for both trading and settling digital assets, marking a significant milestone for blockchain-based financial market infrastructure in Europe.

content: Reading payment data and actually acting upon it are two different concepts in the financial sector. Understanding true customer affordability goes far beyond simply viewing transactional history. Industry experts argue that proper assessment relies heavily on leveraging account information to make informed decisions, ensuring better financial outcomes and supporting customers effectively in managing their financial health.

Google Cloud Outage in London Disrupts Banking and Public Services Across the UK
summary:
A disruption affecting Google Cloud’s London-based infrastructure on October 20 caused technical issues for several banks, financial institutions and public service providers, highlighting the growing reliance on cloud technology across critical services.
Among the affected institutions, UK-based digital bank Revolut experienced service interruptions, with card payments, ATM withdrawals and other services reported as unavailable or partially operational. Germany’s ING also reported difficulties accessing online banking and its mobile application, while Halifax customers encountered problems with digital banking services.
Outage-tracking platform Downdetector recorded reports involving several other organisations, including Lloyds Bank, HSBC, Bank of Scotland, property platform Rightmove, parcel delivery company DPD, NHS England and Royal Mail. The extent of the impact varied across providers, and Lloyds Bank stated that its app remained operational, although some customers were experiencing issues with certain online services.
Google confirmed that its engineering team was investigating the incident affecting its europe-west2 data centre, which primarily serves customers in the UK and Ireland.
Revolut reassured customers about the security of their information and funds, stating: "We can confirm that all our customers' money and data are safe."
The incident also draws attention to growing regulatory scrutiny of financial institutions’ dependence on third-party technology providers. The UK has designated Google Cloud EMEA Limited and three other technology companies as critical third-party suppliers to the financial sector, placing them under direct regulatory oversight. EU regulators have also identified major technology providers whose services are essential to the region’s financial industry.
As banks and public institutions continue to rely on cloud-based infrastructure, the disruption highlights the importance of operational resilience, effective contingency planning and the ability to maintain essential services during technology outages.
Source: Reuters

The incident highlights increasing regulatory scrutiny on the financial sector's reliance on third-party cloud technology providers.

Flex Expands Beyond Rent to Build the Payment Layer for Life’s Financial Obligations
summary:
Flexible Finance, Inc. (“Flex”), the financial technology company building the payment layer for life’s financial obligations, today announced a major expansion of its platform beyond rent. Available immediately, customers can use Flex to manage broadband, car, insurance, mortgage, and utility payments. The expansion builds on a platform that now handles more than $2 billion in payments per month, has served more than 3.5 million customers, and has processed over $45 billion in payments to date. 
Housing and transportation alone—including rent or mortgage, utilities, car payments and insurance—account for roughly half of U.S. consumer spending, or more than $5.3 trillion annually. These payments move through thousands of disconnected apps and websites, each with their own due dates and terms that are often not aligned with paydays, creating a cash-flow challenge no one has solved yet.
“A decade of fintech innovation has transformed almost every part of money management, but it has largely ignored the bills that take up the largest share of household budgets, leaving them fragmented and difficult to manage,” said Shragie Lichtenstein, CEO of Flex. “Rent is where we started, but our vision was always bigger: to build the payment layer for life’s financial obligations and put households back in control of their cash flow."
Today, Flex helps customers avoid more than $39 million in late fees each month and has helped them avoid more than $780 million in total to date. The company applies the same customer-first principles to every bill: transparent pricing, no late fees or penalties charged by Flex, and balances that don’t revolve or compound—plus rent reporting is included to help users build credit history. Before committing, customers see a personalized total based on the bills they choose to pay or split. Pricing includes a $5.99 monthly membership fee and a 0.5% processing fee on all bills paid through Flex. Customers who split a payment also pay a fee of up to 3% of the amount Flex advances. 
The model also creates a more reliable payment relationship between households and billers. By helping billers receive payment in full and on time, Flex can help improve payment performance, reduce the operational burden of collections, and strengthen customer relationships.
Flex's growth is backed by more than $1.5 billion in committed secured borrowing capacity.  If approved, Flex’s bank charter application would allow the company to issue its credit products directly and expand access to its payment solutions through a regulated, FDIC-insured institution.
Consumers can take back control of their cashflow today by downloading the Flex app from the Apple App Store or Google Play. Learn more at getflex.com.
